Just finished a solid run through State of Anarchy and figured I'd drop my thoughts.
This game is pure chaotic dumb fun in the best way possible. It's a top-down shooter where you basically go full GTA psycho mode in a hand-drawn looking town — running people over, blasting everything that moves, stealing cars, and dealing with random alien invasions. The art style is super charming and unique, like someone went wild with markers and crayons. The sound design and over-the-top voice lines had me laughing out loud more than once.
The core gameplay loop is satisfying at first: the shooting feels snappy, driving is decently chaotic, and the levels have that arcade "one more try" energy. It's cheap, it's fast, and it knows exactly what it is — silly anarchic mayhem.
That said, it does wear thin after a while. The game gets pretty repetitive. After you've blown up the same types of enemies and completed a bunch of similar missions, it starts to feel like it's running out of new ideas. Some weapon variety is cool but a lot of it comes down to RNG, and the difficulty can spike in annoying ways or feel too easy depending on your loadout and luck.
It's not a deep game by any means, and it won't keep you hooked for dozens of hours, but for the price it's a fun little time-waster when you want something brain-off and destructive.
If you're in the mood for a short, silly, violent top-down shooter with personality, it's worth picking up on sale. Just don't expect a masterpiece or massive replay value.

State of Anarchy is a highly repetitive top-down shooter with simplistic stick-character or doodle drawings. It initially looks novel, didn't particularly like it myself, but you've quickly seen everything there is to see. Playable with mouse and keyboard. Not really a twin-sick shooter because that would imply proper gamepad support. I didn't like how it controlled, especially with the car, where I constantly got stuck on things. I hated the constantly respawning enemies, but I guess that provoked "anarchy". The game quickly got stale with the same loop every level. Run and/or drive to a bank while killing or avoiding everything in your way. Enter said bank, kill the enemies and reach the level boss at the far end which often has a new weapon. New weapon which you'll use from then on. Rinse and repeat. You cannot select previous weapons. I managed to finish about half the levels before it got too tough for me.

[h1]Anarquía para principiantes: Una reseña de \State of Anarchy\[/h1]

[h2]Resumen[/h2]
¿Alguna vez quisiste lanzarte a la calles, librar las Avenidas de hordas de bandidos con estrafalarios sombreros y disparos que parecen sacados de un dibujo animado hecho por un niño de cinco años? ¡Pues, amigo mío, State of Anarchy es tu tipo de caos! Prepárate para disparar todo lo que se mueva y lo que no, porque, ¿por qué no?

[h2]Aspectos importantes e interesantes[/h2]
Lo primero que salta a la vista, o bueno, lo que intencionadamente trata de hacerte saltar los ojos, son esos gráficos. Parecen sacados de una libreta de bocetos de primaria, pero hey, le dan un estilo único que no encontrarás en otro lado, ¡excepto en el refrigerador de tus padres!

Además, las mecánicas del juego son tan simples que podrías jugarlo mientras te comes un sandwich. Es shooter básico, corre, dispara, añade algo de estrategia del nivel \evitar pisar el Lego\ y voilà, tienes State of Anarchy.

La música es una mezcla rara entre rock pesado, un órgano que encontraron en una venta de garaje y probablemente un kazoo. Sí, es tan anárquico como suena.

[h2]Aspectos por mejorar[/h2]
Por donde empezar... bueno, la dificultad puede oscilar entre \mi abuela podría jugarlo\ y \ok, ¿quién dejó al experto de esports al control?\. Un poco más de balance no le haría mal.

En cuanto a historia, ¿qué historia? Es más o menos como: \Era un día tranquilo y luego, ¡BOOM!, anarquía\. Un poco más de narrativa no estaría mal.

Ahora, necesitamos hablar de la IA. Estos enemigos podrían ganar el premio al enemigo más predecible del año. A veces se quedan atorados en esquinas como Roombas desorientadas.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.
